description: Imports Genesys Cloud contact-center data — users, teams, queues and queue members, outbound and messaging campaigns, plus conversation detail records from the analytics conversation-details async job API.

placeholders.genesys_cloud_domain: the `genesys_cloud_domain` endpoint config field, chosen by the user from a fixed enum of 15 Genesys Cloud regional domains (mypurecloud.com, mypurecloud.ie, mypurecloud.de, mypurecloud.jp, mypurecloud.com.au, usw2.pure.cloud, use2.us-gov-pure.cloud, aps1/apne2/apne3/cac1/euw2/euc2/mec1/sae1.pure.cloud)

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment `/api/v2` appended to the regional host

credentialModes.name: OAuth2 client credentials (customer-registered Genesys Cloud OAuth client)

artifacts: Genesys Cloud asynchronous analytics conversation-details job (created per conversations sweep via POST /api/v2/analytics/conversations/details/jobs; identified by jobId)
continuity.notes: Only the conversations binding creates server-side state, and it is a short-lived analytics job the connector submits, polls to FULFILLED, and drains within a single sweep. Nothing is subscribed to and nothing accumulates on the customer side while we are stopped; the incremental cursor is a datetime, so a long pause is recovered by requesting a wider interval on the next tick. The connector recognises EXPIRED/CANCELLED job states and errors out, but jobs it abandons mid-run are not explicitly deleted.

pathPlaceholders.queueId: id of each parent `queues` record (routing/queues), collected first and iterated in sorted order; the value is also stamped onto each emitted child record as the `queueId` field

authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode is offered: an OAuth2 client_credentials grant where the user supplies client_id and client_secret for an OAuth client they registered themselves in their own Genesys Cloud org. There is no `oauth2` (OAuth2Spec) block in the ConnectorSpec response — only an internal OAuth2TokenFlowSpec used by the connector's own token exchange — so no hosted control plane registers an app on the user's behalf and no browser consent flow exists. No refresh token is ever requested or stored (client_credentials re-mints the access token from the client id/secret each time it nears expiry), so this is not T3. It is above T1 because the user must create and scope an OAuth client rather than paste a single self-serve API key.

unionMisfits.description: The conversations binding is not a single HTTP request with a paginator: it is a three-phase async job protocol. (1) POST analytics/conversations/details/jobs with a JSON body {interval: "<start>/<end>"} returning a jobId; (2) poll GET analytics/conversations/details/jobs/{jobId} on a ~3s backoff until state == FULFILLED, erroring on FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED; (3) GET analytics/conversations/details/jobs/{jobId}/results and cursor-paginate. PullSpec has one path/method/paginator, so the recorded path/method describe phase 1 while recordsPath and paginator describe phase 3. A reader driving the connector from this JSON alone would issue the wrong request sequence.

incrementalParam models a single query parameter carrying a lower bound. Here the window is a single JSON *body* field `interval` holding a slash-joined closed range "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ/YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ" whose upper bound is now(). There is no place in the union to say the parameter is body-borne, that it carries both bounds, or that its format is a range literal rather than a timestamp.

The `page` paginator variant has no tokenTo field in the schema and implicitly assumes query parameters. The teams stream pages a POST search endpoint where pageNumber and pageSize live in the JSON request body, and termination is pageNumber >= pageCount read from the response body. It is neither a clean `page` (wrong send location) nor a `body_cursor` (the value is an incrementing integer the client owns, not a server-issued token). tokenTo: body_field was emitted on a `page` paginator, extending the variant beyond its declared shape.

The list-endpoint loop terminates on two distinct conditions, not one: an empty `entities` array, and a page shorter than the *response-reported* pageSize (the code explicitly treats the response's pageSize as authoritative over the requested 1000, since Genesys silently caps some endpoints). terminateOn is a single enum value, so only short_page is recorded and the response-authoritative page-size detail is lost.

The cursor is not one field. The connector advances the checkpoint to max(conversationEnd, conversationStart) per record — conversationEnd when present, falling back to conversationStart for conversations that have not yet ended — and drops records whose value is <= the previous cursor. cursorField is a single string.

Two different hosts are derived from the same config field: the API host https://api.{domain}/api/v2 and the OAuth token host https://login.{domain}/oauth/token. Only the former fits baseUrl; the latter is recorded on the credentialMode's tokenUrl and is therefore also templated, which the oauth2 scheme's plain-string tokenUrl cannot express.

abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.scopes: The connector never requests or declares OAuth scopes; the token exchange sends only grant_type plus HTTP Basic client credentials. Genesys OAuth clients carry permissions assigned in the customer's org rather than scopes on the request, so no scope list is recoverable from the source. Emitted as an empty list, not an inferred one.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.authUrl: client_credentials grant — there is no browser authorization endpoint. OAuth2TokenFlowSpec carries only accessTokenUrlTemplate; no authUrlTemplate exists on that model (unlike the full OAuth2Spec used by authorization-code connectors).
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No static default headers are set anywhere in the connector. The Authorization header is injected per-request by the CDK's TokenSource; whether the CDK adds anything else (Accept, User-Agent) is a CDK-internal detail not established by connector code.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.tokenPlacement: Not a schema field, but recorded here: client credentials are sent to the token endpoint as HTTP Basic (base64 client_id:client_secret) because the connector selects OAuth2ClientCredentialsPlacement.HEADERS, overriding the CDK default of FORM. The resulting API access token is sent as a bearer token, but the exact prefix comes from the CDK constant DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_TYPE, which was not read.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: The connector never issues a job-delete or cancel call, and nothing in the source says whether Genesys reclaims an abandoned analytics job on its own or how long jobId results remain fetchable. The EXPIRED state proves jobs do expire server-side, but the expiry window is not stated in code.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: The conversations cursor is a plain datetime, which suggests an arbitrarily long pause is recoverable by widening the requested interval, but no code caps the interval width and Genesys's own limit on analytics job interval length is not visible in the connector. Not asserting a window.
abstained.streams[0].pull.backfill: There is no separate historical leg. The single fetch_changes path submits one job spanning cursor -> now on every tick, so the first tick after start_date is the backfill. Recorded entirely under `incremental` rather than duplicated into `backfill`.
abstained.streams[0].supportedSyncModes.pageSizeSe: The results endpoint is called with pageSize=1000 alongside the opaque cursor. Whether Genesys honours pageSize on cursor pages or ignores it is not determinable from the source; the value is reported as pageSize on the cursor paginator without asserting it controls page length.
abstained.streams[*].recordsPath.searchNullResults: SnapshotSearchResponse.results is typed Optional and a falsy value terminates the loop, so an empty-but-present results array and an absent one are indistinguishable in the recorded terminateOn. Reported as explicit_total (pageNumber >= pageCount), which is the loop's other and better-defined exit.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static — the seven bindings are a fixed list in the connector source (FULL_REFRESH_STREAMS plus conversations), confirmed against the discover snapshot. `discover` calls all_resources over that fixed list and performs no remote schema enumeration, so there is no discovery method to describe. Note that record schemas themselves are inferred at runtime (schema_inference=True), which is document-shape inference, not stream discovery.
